what_happened: The job "Keep work and resume on producer deadline; record as timed out" (20261017-044405-4zcq) failed in the producer stage. The producer reached its fixed 1800-second deadline without completing, and the job was recorded as failed. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria, no blocker or major findings and no failed checks. It holds no partial result or last-activity signal, so we cannot tell where the time went. Nothing was delivered. The job's own subject is the fix for this very failure: keeping work and resuming when the producer hits its deadline.
cause: The producer stage has one fixed wall-clock limit, no progress signal, no early stop and no partial result. A timeout therefore discards everything and gives no diagnosis. Nothing before dispatch estimates whether a job fits in one run. The job that adds keep-and-resume is itself exposed to the missing behavior, so the gap blocks its own fix. Retries start without memory of the earlier attempt. The job is also large: it changes how the producer's workspace is kept, how a timeout is recorded, and how the next run resumes. That spans several places and probably exceeds one 1800s run.
prevention: Make a producer timeout a resumable state and not a bare failure. On deadline, Athena would snapshot the producer's working tree and its last activity, record the job as timed out, and let a retry start from that snapshot with a note of what was done. Before dispatch, the planner would also split any job whose plan spans more than one run. For this job, build the keep-and-resume capability in small steps: first record a timeout with the partial diff, then resume from it.
proposed_request: When the producer stage reaches its deadline, Athena should keep the work done so far and let the job resume. Outcome: a job that times out is recorded as "timed out", not as a plain failure. Its working-tree changes and the last activity are saved with the job record. `athena retry` on a timed-out job starts a new producer run from that saved state and tells the producer which files were already changed. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fake producer that exceeds a short deadline shows the job recorded as timed out with the partial diff kept; (2) a test shows retry starts from the kept state and the producer sees the earlier changes; (3) a job that finishes in time behaves as before; (4) existing tests pass. Do only this first step; leave any change to the deadline length for a later job.
